newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - stronger CFDs lead pack higher.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - stronger CFDs lead pack higher.

text.p: European oil swaps were broadly firmer on Thursday, although most gains, barring Brent crude CFDs, were only marginal in a thin market awaiting the U.S open.

Brent CFDs led the pack, gaining support from a physical buyer looking for a cargo. Traders said the the potential buyer had already secured a number of cargoes and the market had thought on Wednesday that the buying spree was complete.
Levels for May 27-30 firmed to 2.5 cents under July compared with 10 cents under on Wednesday, while June 2-6 was pegged around -7.5 cents, compared with - 15 cents yesterday.
Heavy fuel swaps were also pulled higher with June pegged around $84.00 and July in a $1.50-2.00 contango against physical numbers about $1.00 lower.
Traders said there appeared to be a move to keep physical barge levels low, possibly for pricing purposes, and that if swaps started to drift lower there might be strong buying interest.
Low sulphur cargo swaps were steady to 25 cents easier on July. A June swap was traded at $97 with July pegged between $96.75 and $98 with August effectively flat.
Gasoline saw swaps gain by $1-2 a tonne with June around $210. A Eurograde physical barge was sold at $210 fob ARA and a regular barge went for $201.50, both prompt-end May.
Naptha levels were steady around $190.50 for June.
